historical_references.reference: Etemad-e-Solayman, the title of a Persian city, was given by the Seljuq Sultan Sanjar to his capital city of Isfahan in 1050 AD, meaning 'foundation of Solomon'. The city became a significant cultural center and remained the capital until the Mongol invasion in 1220 AD.
Etemad-e-Mohammadi, a title given to the last Safavid Shah, Mohammad Shah, in 1722 AD. He reigned until 1725 AD and was the last ruler of the Safavid Empire before it was overthrown by the Afghans.
